title: A Rivergate for the Monsoon
premise: Petra Voss, a disgraced mountain guide blacklisted from Nepal and Chile after a disaster she refuses to explain, drifts into the coastal town of Rivergate just as an unprecedented tide drains the bay and exposes a sea cave marked with the sigil of a river that appears on no map. When a local cartographer's daughter goes missing following the cave's markings upstream, Petra is the only one who reads them—and the town's powerful harbor trust wants her to fail, or die, so the source stays sealed. Following the river through flooded gorges, abandoned survey camps, and a village that worships the water's memory, Petra discovers the source is a living aquifer the trust has been secretly draining for profit, and that the missing girl's father helped falsify the accident that ruined her. At the climax, Petra must choose between destroying the evidence that would clear her name and opening the sluices that will drown the trust's empire but save the valley; she opens the water, testifies anyway, and finally belongs somewhere—not as a hero, but as the town's reluctant new guide.
about_author: Wren Quintana is the pen name of a former river surveyor who spent a decade mapping waterways across three continents before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people who keep moving, and the rare moments that make them stop.

chapters.title: The Tide That Owed Nothing
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Arriving in Rivergate broke and anonymous, she takes a night shift gutting fish and watches an impossible low tide drain the entire bay. When the water pulls back, a cave mouth yawns open beneath the old lighthouse. The beat is wary curiosity—the instinct to leave warring with the pull to look closer.

chapters.title: Sigils in Salt
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Inside the cave at dawn, she finds survey marks in a cipher she recognizes from her old expedition days—marks that shouldn't exist on this coast. She photographs nothing and tells no one, but a boy, Ilya, has followed her in. The beat is the first crack in her invisibility.

chapters.title: The Harbor Trust
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Trust magistrate Corvane Dall offers her a generous fee to 'verify' the cave is unstable and should be sealed. The money is a trap and she knows it, but she's broke. She takes it. The emotional beat is self-contempt dressed as pragmatism.

chapters.title: What the Cartographer's Daughter Knew
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, the cartographer Odell's sixteen-year-old daughter. Mara has been copying the cave sigils for months from her father's sealed papers and believes they mark a river's true source. She watches Petra report the cave as dangerous and realizes the stranger is lying. The beat is a young person's sharp, dangerous idealism.

chapters.title: A Guide with No Country
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Odell recognizes Petra's name and, instead of exposing her, asks for help: Mara has vanished, leaving a note quoting the sigils. Odell admits the survey marks came from an expedition Petra once led—the one that ended her career. The beat is dread: her past has found her before she could outrun it.

chapters.title: Upstream of Every Map
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra and Odell enter the gorge above the cave, following cairns only she can read. Flashbacks surface in fragments of the disaster: a rope, a storm, a decision she's never spoken aloud. The beat is grief moving at walking pace.

chapters.title: The Village That Remembers Water
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A drowned-valley hamlet, Senn, shelters them; its elders speak of 'the source that breathes' and warn that the Trust's pumps have made the river 'hold its breath.' Petra realizes the river is being drained upstream. The beat is the first sense that her private ruin connects to something larger.

chapters.title: Corvane's Ledger
chapters.summary: Dall's POV. The magistrate reviews the Trust's secret accounts: the aquifer feeding Rivergate has been siphoned for years to power his private syndicate's mills. Mara was seen near the upper pumping station. Dall orders the gorge road closed. The beat is cold, administrative evil—corruption as paperwork.

chapters.title: Rope and Reckoning
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A rockfall traps Odell; Petra must rig a traverse with failing gear, the exact maneuver that failed in her past disaster. She executes it perfectly this time—and admits, aloud, that the original accident was caused by the expedition's funder cutting corners. The beat is confession as survival.

chapters.title: The Girl on the Weir
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Alive, Mara has been hiding at the abandoned survey camp, decoding her father's papers: the source is a living aquifer, and Dall's pumps are killing it—and the valley with it. She leaves a sigil trail for whoever is following. The beat is courage outpacing judgment.

chapters.title: Reunion at the Broken Gauge
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra, Odell, and the Senn elders find Mara at a shattered river gauge. Mara confronts Petra about the cave report; Petra owns the lie. An uneasy alliance forms. The beat is trust being rebuilt from honest wreckage.

chapters.title: The Pumping Station
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The group infiltrates Dall's upper station and finds the scale of the theft: the 'forbidden source' is real, alive, and being bled dry. They also find expedition records proving Dall funded Petra's doomed climb. The beat is fury with nowhere safe to put it.

chapters.title: What Dall Bought
chapters.summary: Odell's POV. Odell confesses he took Trust money years ago to bury the original survey—and that his silence helped Dall frame the accident on Petra's judgment. He begs her forgiveness. The beat is the cost of complicity, paid in front of its victim.

chapters.title: Blacklist, Reconsidered
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. With evidence that could clear her name, Petra faces the choice: publish and clear herself, or use the records as leverage to open the sluices first. Dall's hunters close in. The beat is the theme crystallized—loyalty to the valley versus loyalty to her own vindication.

chapters.title: The Hunt in the Fog Gorge
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A night chase through fog-choked narrows; the elders scatter the hunters with signal fires, and Ilya—who stowed away—nearly drowns saving the evidence satchel. Petra realizes she has a pack now. The beat is belonging arriving unasked.

chapters.title: Corvane's Offer
chapters.summary: Dall's POV. Cornered by his syndicate's falling output, Dall offers Petra full reinstatement, her record wiped, if she seals the source and hands over the records. He genuinely believes he's saving the town from flood. The beat is corruption's last, sincere disguise.

chapters.title: The Source That Breathes
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The group reaches the aquifer cavern: a vast, living chamber of rising and falling water, exactly as the legends charged admission to. Mara's decoded ritual shows the sluices must be opened in sequence or the valley floods. The beat is awe—the moment the adventure becomes a responsibility.

chapters.title: Sluice One
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The opening sequence begins under attack; Odell holds a gate manually, injured, while Petra realizes the final sluice requires someone to stay inside the closing chamber. The beat is sacrifice becoming arithmetic—someone must pay, the only question is who.

chapters.title: The Water Remembers
chapters.summary: Climax. Petra's POV. Petra takes the final chamber herself, opening the last sluice as the aquifer surges free and the Trust's pumps fail forever; the flood spares the valley but drowns Dall's empire, and Dall, refusing rescue, is taken by the water he claimed to serve. The beat is terrible, necessary release.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Weeks later, Petra testifies before an inquiry, telling the whole truth of the original disaster—including her own errors. Her name is cleared, but not glorified; the record stays complicated. The beat is truth chosen over the cleaner version of herself.

chapters.title: A Rivergate for the Monsoon
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The first monsoon in years fills the valley; the town, changed, asks Petra to lead its first guided crossing of the reopened gorge. Mara apprentices under her. The beat is belonging accepted at last—earned, imperfect, and staying.

chapters.title: The Guide Who Stopped
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, epilogue. On the eve of the season, Petra carves the new sigil—her own—beside the old ones in the sea cave, and for the first time in years makes no plans to leave. The beat is quiet arrival: the moving has stopped, and it cost exactly what it was worth.
